questions.stem: A firm wants a model to help review a 200-page contract: a plain-language summary, the sum of the charges it lists, and the decision to proceed. Which split of the work follows the module?

options.text: Claude summarises, code adds the amounts, a lawyer approves the deal
options.says: Summarising is language-shaped work, exact addition belongs to code, and a decision with legal consequences stays with a person (page 1, maths and counting; page 2, the when-not-to table).

options.text: Claude summarises, Claude adds the amounts, a lawyer approves the deal
options.says: Ruled out because exact arithmetic is "approximate unless the model does the work in a tool".

options.text: Claude summarises, code adds the amounts, Claude approves the deal
options.says: Ruled out because the table sends "A decision with legal, medical, financial or safety consequences" to a qualified person.

options.text: Claude summarises and adds the amounts at the highest effort, a lawyer approves the deal
options.says: Ruled out because "The fix is not a better prompt; it is code", and an effort setting is a prompting lever, not a calculator.

questions.stem: A computer-use loop sends full-resolution monitor captures as tool results, and the API refuses some of them. The agent's pointer actions also sometimes land beside their target. What does the documentation support?

options.text: Resend oversized screenshots as they are, and ask in the prompt for better aim
options.says: Ruled out because "Spatial output is approximate", so a prompt line cannot make positions exact, and an unchanged screenshot is refused again.

options.text: Let the API downscale oversized screenshots, and resend any click that missed
options.says: Ruled out because the API "rejects a tool-result screenshot that exceeds the model's limits instead of downscaling it".

options.text: Resize screenshots yourself first, and treat clicks as approximate
options.says: The API rejects an oversized tool-result screenshot instead of downscaling it, so the program resizes first, and spatial output is approximate (page 2, computer use at a glance).

options.text: Move to a model with a larger window, which takes bigger screenshots and aims better
options.says: Ruled out because "Coordinates and localisation outputs are approximate", whatever the model.

questions.stem: A product owner wants an assistant that books flights by operating an airline's website through screenshots and clicks. Which design point matters most for safety?

options.text: Run it in the customer's own browser profile, so saved logins already work
options.says: Ruled out because computer use "runs in an isolated machine, without secrets", and a saved login is exactly such a secret.

options.text: Sandbox it with no credentials, and have a person approve each payment
options.says: Computer use runs in an isolated machine, without secrets, with a person confirming consequential steps (the computer use section).

options.text: Add a prompt line telling it to ignore instructions found on web pages
options.says: Ruled out because "A prompt is a request, not a guarantee", so a line of text cannot replace isolation and confirmation.

options.text: Restrict it to the airline's own site, so its pages can be treated as trusted
options.says: Ruled out because "A screen is untrusted input", and text on any web page can try to give the model instructions.

questions.stem: Which request is the best fit for Claude without extra machinery?

options.text: Checking whether a claim photo is AI-generated, to block fraud
options.says: Ruled out because the vision page says Claude "cannot determine whether an image is AI-generated".

options.text: Calculating the payroll for 800 staff exactly, to the cent
options.says: Ruled out because the table sends "An exact, repeatable result (totals, dates, ids, string edits)" to code.

options.text: Reporting today's closing price of a listed stock
options.says: Ruled out because "Anything recent, private or fast-changing has to come in through the prompt" or a tool, and a live price is after the cut-off.

options.text: Drafting a polite, well-organised reply to a customer's complaint
options.says: Drafting language is the strong-fit row of the summary table, with the usual review for accuracy and fit.
